errors.english: is close at hand sentence continues on next page
errors.why: The words 'sentence continues on next page' are a processing note leaked into the translation, not part of the Tibetan.

fix.find: is close at hand sentence continues on next page

errors.english: the qualifier functions as the means of comprehension
errors.why: ཁྱད་པར་བྱ་བ (likely for ཁྱབ་པར་བྱ་བ) is the qualified / pervaded item that makes the pervader known, not the qualifier (ཁྱད་པར་བྱེད་པ).

note: A careful rendering of a dense vyāpti discussion; apart from a leaked processing note and one bya/byed slip it follows the argument well.
Faithful rendering of the general/specific and literal/figurative characteristics of the four truths; the unmarked inline glosses are a matter of style.

errors.english: are in no way existent entities, because they are not observed in any way whatsoever
errors.why: ཇི་ལྟར་ཡང་ (kathaṃcit) means 'in some respect': the self, pot etc. are in some respect non-existent in nature because in some respect not observed, not 'in no way existent'.

fix.find: are in no way existent entities, because they are not observed in any way whatsoever
fix.replace: are in some respect of a non-existent nature, because in some respect they are not observed

errors.english: are in every way of an existent nature, because they are observed in any way whatsoever
errors.why: Again kathaṃcit: the hare's horn etc. are in some respect existent in nature because in some respect observed, not 'in every way'.

fix.find: are in every way of an existent nature, because they are observed in any way whatsoever
fix.replace: are in some respect of an existent nature, because in some respect they are observed

errors.english: This is because it is observed in any manner whatsoever, whether as a real entity or a non-entity.
errors.why: This is a sample inference (everything, entity or non-entity, is somehow existent because somehow observed) illustrating a one-characteristic reason, not a justification of the preceding sentence.

note: The anyathānupapatti verses are mostly followed, but the Jaina-style 'in some respect' (kathaṃcit) examples are rendered as absolute claims, which inverts their point.

errors.english: "gathering together into one object of focus."
errors.why: འདུ་བ here is samavāya (inherence) and དོན་གཅིག་ལ་འདུ་བ is ekārthasamavāya, 'inherence in a single substrate', a Vaiśeṣika technical term, not 'gathering into one object of focus'.

fix.find: "gathering together into one object of focus."

errors.english: On the other hand, how is fire perceived as fire? By perceiving the common characteristic of sharpness, the mental imprint of fire is awakened.
errors.why: ཇི་ལྟར ... དེ་བཞིན་དུ is 'just as ... so', opening the opponent's analogy, not a question; the clause states that fire was first grasped as fire and then sharpness awakens its imprint.

fix.find: On the other hand, how is fire perceived as fire? By perceiving the common characteristic of sharpness, the mental imprint of fire is awakened.
fix.replace: Objection: just as, when fire has been apprehended as fire and the shared property of sharpness is then apprehended, the latent impression of fire is awakened,

errors.english: Therefore, a single object has many components,
errors.why: The verse says one [cognition] has many objects, as the following line (even while conceptualising one object, others are seen) shows.

note: Follows the anti-Vaiśeṣika argument in outline, but mistranslates samavāya and turns the opponent's fire/brahmin-boy analogy into a question.

errors.english: regarding nocturnal emissions
errors.why: The text speaks of exertion made while lying down / asleep, not of nocturnal emission as such.

note: A competent rendering of difficult Vinaya commentary on the first saṃghāvaśeṣa; a few obscure phrases are interpreted rather than translated but nothing is badly wrong.
Faithful rendering of the Mahāyāna-authenticity argument and the patriarch lineage.

errors.english: "Proof" ends mid-word at page boundary
errors.why: 'ends mid-word at page boundary' is a processing note, not translation.

errors.english: they become vitalized
errors.why: སྐྱེས here is 'gift, present': his words become like a gift when they meet the noble.

errors.english: This is written from the perspective of mastering elegant speech.
errors.why: The sentence begun on the previous side concerns skill in speech that establishes one's own position, not 'elegant' (well-spoken) speech, which is the next verse's topic.

note: The compound-analysis commentary is followed closely; one leaked processing note and a couple of small misreadings.

errors.english: He was born.
errors.why: The subject continues from the previous side: sons were born to the other thirty-four queens too, not 'he' (the prince, whose birth was already narrated).

fix.replace: Sons were born [to the other queens as well].

errors.english: Possessing virtuous qualities and noble intelligence, he became a highly respected and grave figure.
errors.why: This opens a four-line verse (through the ocean/shell simile) that is merged into the prose narrative and partly paraphrased.

errors.english: the regional governor
errors.why: དུམ་བུ་འཛིན་པ is most likely the proper name of the antagonist (who later gathers the brahmins), rendered as a generic title.

note: The narrative line is followed, but the opening misidentifies who was born and the inset verses are flattened into prose.

errors.english: so how could that possibility be averted?
errors.why: ཇི་ལྟར་སྲིད་པ is 'as applicable' (yathāsambhavam): simultaneous or later arising should be refuted as applicable by this same fault; it is an instruction, not a rhetorical question.

note: Good rendering of the Akṣayamati quotation and the unarisen/unceasing argument.

errors.english: had them establish temporary lodgings for him
errors.why: གནས་འཆའ་བ is to take niśraya (formal dependence): Udāyin made the new monks take dependence on him.

fix.find: had them establish temporary lodgings for him
fix.replace: had them take dependence (niśraya) on him

errors.english: The clay materials used for washing should be kept in a pottery shard.
errors.why: ལྕི་བ is cow dung, used as cleansing/plastering material, not clay.

fix.find: The clay materials used for washing
fix.replace: The cow dung used as cleansing material

errors.english: The fifteenth training rule concerning bedding is thus explained.
errors.why: ལྟུང་བྱེད is a pāyantika offence, not a generic 'training rule' (the same applies to the expulsion pāyantika that follows).

errors.english: Except for those [note: grasses] that are clean and not sprouting
errors.why: Continuing སྲོག་ཆགས་ from the previous side, the exception is grass in which living creatures do not breed, not grass that is clean and not sprouting.

note: The narrative of Udāyin is readable, but several Vinaya technical terms (niśraya, pāyantika, cow dung) are mistranslated.
